**Visual observations:**
- Corn leaf showing extensive brown/tan necrotic tissue
- Densely scattered small, discrete, round **black dots/pustules** covering most of the leaf surface
- Some remaining green tissue at the upper margin with yellow halos around some spots
- The black structures appear raised/embedded in the leaf tissue
- No elongated lesions, no powdery pustules, no streaking pattern

**Reasoning:**
The dense scattering of small, circular, raised black structures (stromata) embedded in the leaf tissue is the hallmark of **Tar spot** (*Phyllachora maydis*). These black dots are shiny fungal stromata, distinctly different from:
- Common rust (orange/brown pustules that rupture)
- Gray leaf spot (elongated rectangular lesions)
- Northern corn leaf blight (large cigar-shaped lesions)
- Physoderma brown spot (has a distinct band pattern, no black dots like this)

The appearance here -- hundreds of small, round, black, raised dots on a browning leaf -- is classic tar spot.
